correctness.rationale: The exact finite selector identity reduces the centered graph-ball maximal-operator squared l2 norm to max_lambda(A_sigma^T A_sigma) over every 4^n radius mask for n=6,7. I independently reconstructed the 30- and 105-scaled averaging matrices. Exact integer Bareiss/Sylvester checks enumerated all 4096 C6 masks and all 16384 C7 masks: respectively exactly 12 and 7 dihedral winners, with 4084 and 16377 strict losing inequalities at 1.517 and 1.531. Exact integer Rayleigh witnesses exceed 1.520400 and 1.532672; positive-definite upper isolations at 1.520401 and 1.532673, Gram characteristic coefficients and announced quintic/cubic are verified. Uniform-ball rows make the winning Grams entrywise positive, so Perron simplicity fixes the modulus; arbitrary coordinate signs/phases are permitted because M uses |f|. This proves precisely two cycles, real and complex, not a larger-cycle family.

value.rationale: The six- and seven-cycles are the first natural diameter-three cycle pair, with distinct parity and different equality orbits. Exact algebraic Hilbert maximal norms and ALL extremizers supply a nontrivial finite extremal benchmark; the result is not a mere recomputation of the norm of a fixed linear averaging operator because it optimizes all 20,480 nonlinear row selections. Its bounded scope is explicit, and no claim of a universal cycle theorem is made.

scientific_limitations: No assertion for n>=8, weighted cycles, or uncentered operators.
Exact exhaustive arithmetic covers only these two graphs; literature search cannot prove global uniqueness of historical priority.
